class.name: Texture2D
class.description: A texture works by registering an image in the video hardware, which then can be used in 3D models or 2D [Sprite2D] or GUI [Control]. Textures are often created by loading them from a file. See [method @GDScript.load]. [Texture2D] is a base for other resources. It cannot be used directly. [b]Note:[/b] The maximum texture size is 16384×16384 pixels due to graphics hardware limitations. Larger textures may fail to import.

method.name: _draw
method.description: Called when the entire [Texture2D] is requested to be drawn over a [CanvasItem], with the top-left offset specified in [param pos]. [param modulate] specifies a multiplier for the colors being drawn, while [param transpose] specifies whether drawing should be performed in column-major order instead of row-major order (resulting in 90-degree clockwise rotation). [b]Note:[/b] This is only used in 2D rendering, not 3D.

method.name: _draw_rect
method.description: Called when the [Texture2D] is requested to be drawn onto [CanvasItem]'s specified [param rect]. [param modulate] specifies a multiplier for the colors being drawn, while [param transpose] specifies whether drawing should be performed in column-major order instead of row-major order (resulting in 90-degree clockwise rotation). [b]Note:[/b] This is only used in 2D rendering, not 3D.

method.name: _draw_rect_region
method.description: Called when a part of the [Texture2D] specified by [param src_rect]'s coordinates is requested to be drawn onto [CanvasItem]'s specified [param rect]. [param modulate] specifies a multiplier for the colors being drawn, while [param transpose] specifies whether drawing should be performed in column-major order instead of row-major order (resulting in 90-degree clockwise rotation). [b]Note:[/b] This is only used in 2D rendering, not 3D.

method.description: Draws the texture using a [CanvasItem] with the [RenderingServer] API at the specified [param position].

method.name: get_format
method.description: Returns the image format of the texture.

method.name: get_height
method.description: Returns the texture height in pixels.

method.name: get_image
method.description: Returns an [Image] that is a copy of data from this [Texture2D] (a new [Image] is created each time). [Image]s can be accessed and manipulated directly. [b]Note:[/b] This will return [code]null[/code] if this [Texture2D] is invalid. [b]Note:[/b] This will fetch the texture data from the GPU, which might cause performance problems when overused. Avoid calling [method get_image] every frame, especially on large textures. [b]Note:[/b] On the web, a read from the GPU cannot wait for the data. For a texture whose pixels are on the GPU (a [ViewportTexture], a [Texture2DRD], a [DrawableTexture2D], or an [ImageTexture] in an exported project), the first call returns [code]null[/code], and a later call returns what the previous call copied, a frame or more old. Use [method get_image_async] instead, which calls back once the pixels have arrived and behaves the same on every platform.

method.name: get_image_async
method.description:
Reads this texture back and calls [param callback] with an [Image] of its pixels once they have arrived, or with [code]null[/code] if the texture is invalid, is freed before the data arrives, or the read fails. [param callback] is called exactly once per call, later, on the main thread; never from inside this method. For a texture whose pixels are on the GPU (a [ViewportTexture] from [method Viewport.get_texture], a [Texture2DRD], a [DrawableTexture2D], an [ImageTexture]), the copy is made once the current frame has been drawn, so the image is what this frame rendered, even when called from [method Node._ready]. It arrives a few frames later (see [member ProjectSettings.rendering/rendering_device/vsync/frame_queue_size]) without stalling the GPU, unlike [method get_image]. Requests complete in the order they were made. The result is the same on every platform, including the web, where [method get_image] cannot wait for the GPU. Other textures call back with what [method get_image] returns. [codeblock] func save_screenshot(): get_viewport().get_texture().get_image_async(func(image: Image): if image: image.save_png("user://screenshot.png")) [/codeblock] To [code]await[/code] the image, have the callback emit a signal: [codeblock] signal image_read(image: Image)
func capture() -> Image: get_viewport().get_texture().get_image_async(image_read.emit) return await image_read [/codeblock] [b]Note:[/b] Every function awaiting [code]image_read[/code] resumes on its next emission, so with this pattern keep one request per signal in flight at a time. [b]Note:[/b] The copy is made when a frame is drawn. If nothing is drawn (for example, the window is minimized while [member OS.low_processor_usage_mode] is enabled), the callback waits for the next frame that is.
